text:
incident-bot: Pager - hf storage 503s affecting model artifact fetches for runtime-model-loader. Paging on-call: jamie. Severity: P1.

jamie: ack, on it. seeing spikes in model-load errors and cold-start failures. route: hosted models -> hf.co artifacts.

sara: logs: we started getting HTTP 503s from https://huggingface.co/models/rdw/quant-sm/resolve/main/ggml-quant.bin ~11:02 UTC. repeated timeouts when pulling blobs during scale-up.

alex: metrics: 5xx for /v1/generate up ~7% last 10m, cold-start errors (artifact_fetch_fail) ~22% for new containers. heap of retry attempts piling up.

jamie: immediate mitigation plan:
1) disable new cold-starts for affected model by pinning traffic to cached variant (quant-sm:v1-cached).
2) bump fetch retry backoff and limit to avoid thundering herd.
3) enable local in-memory artifact cache for the next 30m.
4) open support ticket with Hugging Face and request rate-lift / status.
5) communicate degraded latency to customers for affected routes.

tyler: doing step 1 now — updating routing policy.

deploy-bot: routing policy updated: model rdw/quant-sm -> rdw/quant-sm:v1-cached (100%) by tyler at 11:08 UTC.

jamie: step 2: increasing fetch retry backoff in runtime config. Patch applied to model-loader config:
```yaml
model_fetch: 
  retries: 6
  base_backoff_ms: 300
  max_backoff_ms: 8000
```
Rolling restart of small subset of loaders to pick change.

sara: curl sample showing HF 503:
```bash
curl -I https://huggingface.co/rdw/quant-sm/resolve/main/ggml-quant.bin
HTTP/2 503
date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:03:12 GMT
content-type: application/json
content-length: 70
{ "error": "Service temporarily unavailable - storage throttled" }
```

jamie: opened HF ticket (internal ref: HF-9882) and pasted logs + traffic patterns. hf-support-bot: created ticket #HF-9882, status: open, assigned to hf-ops.

hf-support-bot: HF acknowledged spike and asked for sample request IDs and timestamps. They are checking CDN origin throttles.

alex: customer impact calc (rough): ~4% of hosted requests returned degraded responses or higher latency, ~0.5% hard failures where model couldn't be loaded and fallback model used. Affected customers: interactive playground + subset of low-traffic hosted API keys. Dedicated customers with pinned artifacts mostly fine.

jamie: communications: post a short status in #general and send targeted email to customers with affected model ids. I'll draft after handoff.

tyler: starting warmers to prefetch cached variant into warm pool to avoid future cold starts. warming jobs launched (50 instances).

deploy-bot: warming jobs created: prefetcher/quant-sm-cache x50.

sara: after routing change and warmers, artifact_fetch_fail rate dropped from 22% -> 6% over 12 minutes. API 5xx back to +1.5% over baseline.

jamie: good. still waiting for HF confirmation on permanent fix. leaving note for handoff: I'll hand to alex in 30m for overnight monitoring. key actions for next oncall: monitor artifact_fetch_fail metric, check HF ticket updates, keep cached routing until HF says healthy.

alex: ack takeover at 11:40 UTC. will keep pinned routing and schedule cache TTL extension to 2h to reduce re-fetch pressure.

tyler: pushed cache-ttl change to 2h for cached variants.

hf-support-bot: HF update: origin CDN experienced transient overload due to a region-level storage failover, mitigation in progress; recommending backoff + CDN retry. Estimated resolution: 45-90m.

jamie: customer comms sent: short note explaining degraded artifact availability causing higher cold-start latency, listing mitigations and ETA. link to support page. (msg id: cm-7908)

alex: handoff complete. next checks: metric trend at +15m, HF ticket updates. leaving this thread for postmortem if HF doesn't confirm clean.

jamie: thanks all — closing paging loop for now. will reopen if regressions. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Pager closed for jamie.

(End of thread)
